solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Top bloke has reserve

parts.note: bod is informal British slang for a person or fellow
ice is coolness of manner, reserve or aloofness

explanation.surface: A man at the head of something keeps himself to himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' looks like an adjective about a leading bloke, but it is a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A close-fitting garment covering the upper body is a type of women's top.

clue.text: Formally ask heads for better English grades

indicators.note: the heads of the following words are their first letters

explanation.surface: A pupil makes a formal request for higher English marks.
explanation.definitionFit: To plead or request earnestly, as in 'I beg your pardon', is a formal way of asking.

clue.text: Lower classes take frivolous pleasure

parts.note: D and E are the lowest grades in the British social classification of occupations
light means not serious, trivial

explanation.surface: Working-class people indulge in some lightweight fun.
explanation.walkthrough: British market research grades households A, B, C1, C2, D, E; D and E are the lower classes.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are nouns for great enjoyment or happiness, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Shut up barracks where there is hand-to-hand fighting

parts.note: to close is to shut up, as a shop at night
quarters is soldiers' lodging, as barracks are

explanation.surface: Troops are confined to barracks where brawling breaks out.
explanation.definitionFit: Fighting at very short range, body to body, is fighting at close range, the phrase's usual sense.

clue.text: Something ejected from place included in total

indicators.note: one word is enclosed within the letters of the other, as if included in it

parts.note: a sum is a total
to put is to place

explanation.surface: An item thrown out of a location is counted in the overall figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Phlegm or spit coughed up from the lungs is matter expelled from the body.

clue.text: Heavily attack reliable currency

parts.note: to pound is to bombard or batter
sterling means dependable, of solid worth

explanation.surface: Speculators hammer a sound currency.
explanation.definitionFit: The British pound is the money of the United Kingdom, a national currency.

clue.text: Time wasted over valuable find

indicators.note: wasted suggests something ruined or wrecked, so these letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Time spent searching proves pointless, then a treasure turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reads as a direction word, but 'wasted' scrambles it; 'Time' is the single letter at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A trove is a store of treasure discovered, as in treasure trove.

clue.text: Plant recycled materials

indicators.note: recycled material is broken down and remade, so these letters are reformed

explanation.surface: A factory reuses old stock.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a name for a water plant, Hippuris, and also for horsetail, so it is a botanical example.

clue.text: Up and about in a prison

parts.note: stir is slang for prison

explanation.surface: An inmate is already awake and moving around inside a jail.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means stirring, out of bed and active, the same sense as the phrase.

clue.text: Would it make you die laughing?

definitions.text: Would it make you die laughing?

parts.words: Would it make you die laughing?
parts.note: dying laughing normally means great amusement; here it is jokes made at an execution, comedy of a grim kind

explanation.surface: A question asking whether something is fatally funny.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for helpless laughter is read literally: laughter tied to a death by hanging.
explanation.definitionFit: Grim, macabre jokes about death or disaster are named after the scaffold where criminals were hanged.

clue.text: Yank's stomach turned over

indicators.note: turned over means flipped round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: gut is the stomach

explanation.surface: An American feels queasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yank' looks like an American with an upset stomach; it is the verb meaning pull.
explanation.definitionFit: To yank is to give a sharp pull, which is what a tug is.

clue.text: Jam leggings over stomach

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits above, over, the second

parts.note: tights are leg coverings
pot is a paunch, as in pot belly

explanation.surface: Pulling leggings up over a belly is a squeeze.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a jam is being in a difficult predicament, the same idiom.

clue.text: I resolved to smash criminals

indicators.note: smashing breaks things to pieces, so these letters are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Someone vows to break up a crime ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrongdoers who commit wicked acts are lawbreakers, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Leave some mangetouts

indicators.note: some of the word means just part of its letters are taken

explanation.surface: Abandon a portion of the pea pods on the plate.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means go away or depart, as in an order to leave.

clue.text: I sat shocked, receiving bill for sports grounds

indicators.note: one set of letters takes the other inside it
shocked suggests being shaken up, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: ad, short for advertisement, is a bill or poster

explanation.surface: A diner is stunned to be handed the bill at the stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shocked' rearranges I SAT into ST IA, and 'receiving' takes AD into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of stadium in its Latin form, so sports arenas.

clue.text: In river, simple craft one conscripted

indicators.note: the craft is placed in the river, inside its letters

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland, and another on the English-Welsh border
a raft is a basic boat

explanation.surface: A recruit is sent down a river on a basic boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A person drafted into the armed forces is a conscript.

clue.text: One author, or two

definitions.meaning: Mark ..., the pen name of Samuel Clemens, the American writer
an old word for two, as in 'never the ... shall meet'

explanation.definitionFit: The archaic word for a pair doubles as the surname of the writer of Huckleberry Finn.

clue.text: Biggest attraction is of the highest class

definitions.meaning: read as ..., the thing that draws the most people
an idiom for first-rate, of the best social standing

explanation.surface: The star exhibit is a cut above.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally the uppermost drawer, where the best things are kept, hence excellent; cryptically the best puller of crowds.

clue.text: Earlier, pair drinking port

indicators.note: one piece takes the other in, as if swallowing it

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port

explanation.surface: Before this, two people were sipping fortified wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' reads as the drink but is a harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means coming before in time, previous.

clue.text: What makes a hole in everything, we're told

indicators.note: we're told means heard spoken, so a word with the same sound is used

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: A riddle about something that punctures everything.
explanation.definitionFit: A pointed tool used for piercing leather or wood makes holes.

clue.text: Coach clergyman to become senior politician

parts.note: to prime is to prepare or brief someone
a minister is a member of the clergy

explanation.surface: Train a vicar to rise to high office.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of government in Britain is its most senior politician.

clue.text: Free trip cut short

indicators.note: the word is shortened by losing its last letter

parts.note: a ride is a journey or trip

explanation.surface: A complimentary journey ends early.
explanation.definitionFit: To rid is to clear or free, as in rid of pests.

clue.text: Severely criticise introducing husband in party

indicators.note: the single letter is introduced into the other word

parts.note: to trash something is to slate it

explanation.surface: Someone lays into a man for bringing her spouse to a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Severely criticise' looks like the definition; it is TRASH, and 'party' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a thrash is a lively party or celebration.

clue.text: A good saxophone, for one, was in harmony

parts.note: a saxophone is an example of a reed instrument

explanation.surface: A fine sax kept in tune with the band.
explanation.definitionFit: To have agreed is to have concurred, the same sense as being in accord.
